Sonia’s memoir ‘Belonging’ debuts with 2 lakh copies sold in under a week: HarperCollins India CEO
 The thunderous response to the book has clearly taken even the debut author by surprise, with Sonia Gandhi admitting that she is “overwhelmed” by the outpouring of love and affection from readers
 Updated - November 17, 2026 12:30 am IST - New Delhi 
 PTI READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Congress Parliamentary Party Chairperson Sonia Gandhi speaks during the launch of her memoir, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, in New Delhi on November 17, 2026.
 | Photo Credit: X/@INCIndia via ANI
 From dominating headlines since its announcement in August to flying off bookstore shelves, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s memoir has had a blockbuster run, with HarperCollins India CEO Ananth Padmanabhan saying it has sold “over two lakh copies” in less than a week, broken multiple publishing records and emerged as one of the “biggest memoirs” in independent India’s history.
 Sonia Gandhi’s ‘Belonging’: From being shelved to the shelves “Belonging: A Journey of Love”, officially launched at a packed event at ITC Maurya in New Delhi on Monday (November 16, 2026), was attended by the who’s who of the Congress and the INDIA opposition bloc, literary figures and a host of Chief Ministers, including Tamil Nadu’s C. Joseph Vijay, Karnataka’s D.K. Shivakumar and Himachal Pradesh’s Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu.
 Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi, Party General Secretary (Organisation) K. C. Venugopal, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, Jammu and Kashmir CM Omar Abdullah, People’s Democratic Party (PDP) Chief Mehbooba Mufti and other leaders during the launch event of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, in New Delhi.
 | Photo Credit: 
 X/@INCIndia via ANI
 Celebrating the book’s unprecedented sales, Mr. Padmanabhan said it has already set several publishing records — and clearly not one at a time — with more than two lakh copies sold in less than a week after going on sale at 10 a.m. last Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
 “With more than two lakh copies sold in less than a week, the book has broken many records already: it is the fastest-selling book, the fastest-selling debut, the fastest-selling work of non-fiction and the fastest-selling memoir,” he said.
 More than “15,000 copies” were also delivered in under 10 minutes on the day of publication, making it the fastest-delivered book in the country’s publishing history, he added.
 Review | Sonia Gandhi’s Belonging: A memoir of revelation and reticence The thunderous response to the book has clearly taken even the debut author by surprise, with Ms. Gandhi admitting that she is “overwhelmed” by the outpouring of love and affection from readers.
 “I always thought people would be impressed within certain weeks, but this has been overwhelming, unexpected and overwhelming,” Ms. Gandhi said.
 “I am deeply touched by the love and affection people have shown in their comments, in buying the book and even in the critiques. Those are the reasons,” the Congress Parliamentary Party chief said with a smile, drawing thunderous applause from the packed hall, including from her children — Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and AICC general secretary Priyanka Gandhi.
 Initially slated to be published in India by Penguin Random House, the memoir found a new publisher, HarperCollins India, after the author and the former publishing house failed to reach an agreement over certain editorial changes.
 Related Stories
 While Congress leaders alleged pressure to remove politically-sensitive references, Penguin denied any external interference, maintaining that the disagreement was part of its regular editorial process.
 With the book now breaking sales records, Mr. Padmanabhan and the team at HarperCollins India are clearly laughing all the way to the bank. However, Padmanabhan remained tight-lipped about how HarperCollins India came on board, saying it is a “story for another day”.
 He did reveal, though, that the publishing house had “less than 12 weeks” to bring the book to readers.
 In a lighter moment, Mr. Padmanabhan quipped that there are now only three kinds of people in India — “those who bought the book and read it, those who bought the book and are waiting for it to be delivered and those who bought the book, read it, but do not have the courage to admit it.”
 “Belonging: A Journey of Love” is a personal memoir, with politics providing the background or “a kind of framework”, as Gandhi writes in the book.
